purpose: Records the current code would decide differently from their committed form and that need the models or a decision to be settled. The RAG step, replayed offline on the committed caches, now reports a figure or reaches the page-vision step, and the committed record was written without it. Until each is extracted again it keeps its committed form; scripts/restate_record_status.py leaves these records alone, and the corpus replay check reads this list as its declared exceptions. Since 3 October 2026 (stage 2 of the fix cycle for the review of 2 October 2026) it also lists records whose stored table triangle the report-year diagonal rule refuses and that cannot be rebuilt offline. Sixteen were declared on that day. Twelve page-vision calls (option B of the stage-2 decision, 3 October 2026) served eleven of them, and ten of those were regenerated and left the list. Six remain. 2999/2022's page reading disagrees with its page and is not used. 2121/2019 and 3622/2023 have only a response to the same prompt from an older driver version, which the cache does not serve and which is not asked for again. 1967/2014, 1991/2018 and 3500/2018 would be written as no deterministic reading and leave the working sample, which is a decision for the author; 1400/2014, whose page reading held no triangle, was regenerated as no deterministic reading; it did not leave the working sample, as it was never in it (the analysis excluded it as a run-off year). Each of the six keeps its committed form until its figure is registered from its page or the decision is made. 2999/2022's declaration stays on this list while its committed figure (375.6) differs from its replay (+858.1, from the served reading): taking it off sends the replay red, and refusing the shifted grid or taking the cache entry out of service changes only what the replay differs by. It ends when the record, regenerated from a correct reading of the page, carries the page's +370.5 and so agrees with its replay.

extracted.note: the 13 records extracted again one at a time with the models (prompt 2.13, --batch, Azure cache only, no table-backend call); each was read against its filing page afterwards. The $0.2732 (the sum of the records' total_cost_usd) is the price of the run's 24 whole-document calls only: it leaves out the Gemini thinking tokens those calls recorded and the run's page-vision calls (8 cached responses), whose cost was not recorded (see cost).

cost.counts: the 24 whole-document calls, gemini-2.5-flash and gpt-5-mini for each of the 12 records that reached the models (1985/2024 became a first-year stub before them): the sum of those records' total_cost_usd, each the sum of its two responses' cost_usd, which test_gemini prices from PRICING and the input and output token counts the response recorded. It is the price table's figure, not a provider's bill.
cost.gemini_tokens_not_priced_note: the 12 gemini-2.5-flash whole-document responses record 76,473 tokens in total_tokens beyond their input and output counts (the model's thinking tokens); the price formula prices the input and output counts only, so these tokens are not in the $0.2732. The gpt-5-mini responses record no such difference.
cost.page_vision_note: the run's page-image calls to gemini-2.5-flash, known from their responses: the 8 page-level llm_cache entries written for these records on 2026-09-29 (pages numbered from 1). A response that fails to parse is not cached, so a call retried after one would not show here. The page-level cache keeps the triangle only, not the token usage, and the page-vision cost reaches neither a record's total_cost_usd nor the run total, so the cost of these calls was not recorded. 1985/2024 made no whole-document call, and its stub records no cost.
